picks.why: colored bird’s-eye view of the walled harbor town on the Zuiderzee; flat single-sheet copy; legend block at right trimmed

picks.what: View from the Zuiderzee with the stone beacon, drawing (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: dated true view of the town from the water, church spire and beacon visible; light gray wash, so the town is a thin strip

notes: Braun and Hogenberg Enkhuizen is in vol. 3 (1581); #1 and #3 are bound spreads with the gutter through the town, #4 is a flat sheet. Kieser’s Sciographia Cosmica profile view (#6, 1637–38) is a good small alternative for P1. P2: Pompe (#8) is a ship painting with the town as a speck, dated only ‘17th century’; Merian (#7) is a street plan. #9 is faint; keep it only if a weak 18th-century view is better than none. #10 is labeled on the plate as Medemblik although the Rijksmuseum titles it Enkhuizen, so skipped. #5’s ‘1515’ is a shelf mark (Eversen, 19th century). P4: Nieuwenkamp’s 1912 etching of the Drommedaris (#15) is a possible second P4. #23 is the Krabbersgat naviduct, #24 a single shed, #25 a crop of #22.
